originals.why: No 'ydy o'n' here: 'ydy' is followed by 'beth', and "o'n" belongs to "o'n i" (I was). The phrase never uses the LEGO 'whether it is'.

originals.ko: ~은 그들이 우리 앞에 있지 않다는 거야
originals.why: "o'n" here is part of "o'n blaenau ni" (in front of us), not "ydy o'n" (whether it is). Wrong sense of the LEGO.

originals.ko: 나는 그게 사실인지 확실하지 않지만 내가 그에게 물어볼게
그가 무엇을 말하든 그건 내 거야
originals.why: No 'ydy o'n' here: the line has "mae o'n" and 'ydy hwnnw'. The LEGO is not used.
'sut beth ydy o' has 'ydy o' with no 'yn', meaning 'what it's like'. That is not the LEGO "ydy o'n" (whether it is).

topups.why: A bare 'wnest ti' statement is odd in Welsh, and the Korean reads as a question. Weaker than the two kept.
Grammatical, but not needed: only 2 were wanted.
Not needed; the Korean 틀린지 should also be 틀렸는지.
After 'do'n i ddim yn gwybod', the past 'os oedd o'n' is more natural than 'os ydy o'n'.
Very close to the seed and long; not needed.

originals.ko: 너 어젯밤 빠른 차 소리를 들었어?
나는 무서워 왜냐하면 나는 어젯밤 빠른 차 소리를 들었거든
